subject: Materials Science
title: The Electrochemical Cell
description: A quick, practical guide to The Electrochemical Cell.

hook.text: A battery produces electricity from corrosion — the zinc case dissolves to power your flashlight.

buildup.text: A corrosion cell has an anode where metal dissolves and a cathode where a reduction reaction occurs.

discovery.text: Electrons flow from anode to cathode through the metal. Ions flow through the electrolyte to close the circuit.

twist.text: Remove any one component — anode, cathode, electrolyte, or conductor — and corrosion stops.

climax.text: Understanding the corrosion cell is how engineers design protection — break the circuit, stop the damage.

punchline.text: Corrosion is a battery you never wanted — prevention is pulling the plug.

quiz.question: What happens at the anode in a corrosion cell?
